CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and has not married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service providers are every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 21

1. Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Safe Houses etc)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 27

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of Violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 23

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services for:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD that oversees Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or community organizations in the social field that already exist; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

Article 30

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration is intended so that:

a.women victims of Violence can resume their social life; and

b.women victims of Violence can have a decent life.  (3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women

Article 48

1. Regional Government is obligated to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking; and (3) Regional Government, community, family and parents are obligated to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 29

1. Repatriation is intended to return women victims of Violence to their Region of origin.
2. Repatriation of women victims of Violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 65

Service efforts carried out by the Regional Government for child victims of acts of Violence as referred to in Articles 42 through 64 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for child victims of acts of Violence.

Article 46

1. Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
2. Every Child has the right to receive Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 66

1. Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children: a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and Children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and has not married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Article 32

1. Employers who employ women must maintain decency, safety and security while at the workplace.
2. Employers must place women workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of women workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  (4) Employers must provide special breastfeeding facilities at their company.

Article 33

1. Women workers/laborers under 18 (eighteen) years of age are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy.
3. Employers who employ women workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must:a. provide nutritious food and drinks; andb. maintain decency and security while at the workplace.
4. Employers must provide shuttle transportation for women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women

Article 21

1. Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Safe Houses etc)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 23

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services for:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD that oversees Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or community organizations in the social field that already exist; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

Article 30

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration is intended so that:

a.women victims of Violence can resume their social life; and

b.women victims of Violence can have a decent life.  (3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 32

1. Employers who employ women must maintain decency, safety and security while at the workplace.
2. Employers must place women workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of women workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  (4) Employers must provide special breastfeeding facilities at their company.

Article 33

1. Women workers/laborers under 18 (eighteen) years of age are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy.
3. Employers who employ women workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must:a. provide nutritious food and drinks; andb. maintain decency and security while at the workplace.
4. Employers must provide shuttle transportation for women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service providers are every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30.

General

Article 54

Regional Government conducts periodic supervision of every person/entity that employs Children in efforts to Protect child workers.

Article 48

1. Regional Government is obligated to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of Violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women

Article 21

1. Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Safe Houses etc)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.

Article 66

3. Community participation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 23

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.

a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD that oversees Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or community organizations in the social field that already exist; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and has not married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service providers are every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 23

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services for:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD that oversees Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or community organizations in the social field that already exist; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

Article 48

1. Regional Government is obligated to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking; and (3) Regional Government, community, family and parents are obligated to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 47

1. Children with disabilities and Children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including inclusive education programs.
2. Regional government provides teaching staff for inclusive education at every education unit.
